title: skills route mis-routes a generic review request to a specialist, and orient never reads the prompt

AC1.note: routing-baseline.ts carries 24 pairs including every negative the AC names — commitment issues, pushback from the team, preview the deck, проверь почту, проверка почты, open the file — each with its recorded top and a verdict, so the corpus records what the router gets WRONG as well as right. Landed in #436 before the scorer changed, which is the ordering the AC exists to enforce. 64 routing tests pass.

AC2.note: The inflected forms the AC names are all present with the current scorer's behaviour recorded: run the deployment -> deploy 65, reviewing the diff now -> review-orchestrator 55, commits are failing -> commit 40, brainstorming ideas -> brainstorm 85, interviewing me first -> interviewer 55.

AC3.note: Every pair is ranked through scoreBundledSkillRoute, the function the CLI calls, and routing-baseline.test.ts carries a test asserting no second copy of the ranking exists. The two guards added for AC5 and AC9 follow the same rule: AC5 ranks through the same scorer, AC9 spawns the real CLI.

AC4.note: Fixed in #436, verified by running the CLI from source at this HEAD: 'review' -> review-orchestrator 65, 'review the PR' -> 65, 'do a full review without fixing' -> 75, and the Russian 'сделай мне полное ревью без исправления' -> review-orchestrator 75, which previously returned review-frontend 65 and did not list the orchestrator in the top ten. A request naming a specialist still reaches it: 'frontend review' -> review-frontend 75, 'security review' -> review-security-code 75.

AC5.note: src/commands/trigger-reachability.test.ts enumerates every catalog trigger and pins the SET with no order-free path by name, not by count — 11 to 17 is visible in a count, but which six is the question, and a count also hides one trigger regaining a path while another loses it. The recorded set is empty today. Proved not vacuous: reinstating the first attempt's rule (deny the order-free path to any trigger that lost a word to the three-character filter) strands 36 triggers, the snapshot names every one, and the concrete 'ui review' case fails separately.

AC6.note: Verified by running: no single Russian word satisfies a multi-word trigger, and route-synonyms.test.ts carries a named test that проверь means check and specifically does not mean review. The baseline records the consequence honestly rather than hiding it — 'проверка почты' and 'проверь почту' land on docpack-review at 20, marked verdict:wrong with the note that провер no longer implies review so nothing confident answers.

AC7.note: route-synonyms.test.ts asserts each family as a closed contract: expected tokens present AND named routing-hot tokens absent, plus a test that no family quietly produces a routing-hot token it never claimed. That is the addition case the first attempt's table test could not see.

AC8.note: DECISION, not an implementation: keryx orient was NOT taught to read the prompt, so the conditional this AC opens with does not fire and there is no routing block to fold before runtime.format. Established rather than assumed — src/commands/orient.ts contains exactly one occurrence of the word prompt, in a comment describing the install-hook subcommand. Teaching orient to read prompts is a feature with its own design, not a side effect of a routing repair, and the first attempt's version of this AC was confirmed against code that was later removed. Recorded as out of scope with the reason, which is what the AC asks for when the condition is false.

AC9.note: The per-prompt router DOES include project-skills, so the first branch applies and emission is proved rather than excluded. The inert filter is gone: the code filters on score > 0, not on the phantom trigger reason scoreProjectSkillRoute never emits. Verified end to end through the CLI against the real registry of two entries — 'init command' returns init-command at 280 with source project, 'gdgraph module' returns module at 310. Pinned by src/commands/project-skill-routing.test.ts in both directions, since a router that returned a project row for every query would satisfy the positive case alone.

AC10.note: Both guards added by this flow are mutation-verified. AC5's guard: reinstating the first attempt's order-free denial strands 36 triggers and fails two named tests, the snapshot and the 'ui review' case. AC9's guard: the negative test fails if the router emits a project row for a query naming nothing. The AC1-AC3 corpus was mutation-verified in #436 when it landed.

AC11.note: bunx tsc --noEmit: 0 errors. bun run lint: clean. 71 routing tests pass across the five files. Full suite run at the end of this branch introduces no failure beyond what reproduces on origin/main.

Routing work removed from PR #431 in ff0ea1e6 and returned to design. Round 3 measured the change as net-negative: word-boundary padding removed 29 one-word triggers' inflected matching (run the deployment / reviewing the diff now / commits are failing all went to SILENCE); asymmetric trigger tokenisation took order-free matching from 11 triggers to 17 (15 lost, 9 gained); провер lost its review mapping while the sibling stem проверк kept it; routePrompt's project-skill inclusion is inert because it filters on a trigger reason that scoreProjectSkillRoute never emits. ROOT CAUSE, and the reason this is a redesign rather than a fix: the corpus had NO NEGATIVE PAIRS, so every round could see improvements and none could see losses. AC1-AC11 are confirmed against code that is no longer on the branch — treat them as void. Restart condition: build the corpus with negative pairs (queries expected to route to nothing, plus inflected forms of every one-word trigger) FIRST, then change the scorer. The diagnosis is sound and unchanged: review-frontend's 'ui review' trigger degenerates to ['review'] and hijacks every review request in every language.
